title: Your pencils
hint: HB, 2B and 6B (or any 3B-6B), plus a white eraser.
say: Three pencils today: an H-B for your lightest greys, a two-B for the mid-tones, and a six-B for your darkest darks -- any pencil from three-B to six-B works there, so use whatever you have sharp. You'll also want a tissue for blending, and a white eraser -- or an eraser pencil, or a kneaded eraser pinched to a point -- for lifting highlights. Keep all three pencils sharp; we'll stop to sharpen more than once.

title: A tissue for blending
say: A small tissue blends your shading smooth once the tone is built up. We'll get there in a few steps -- for now, just know it's coming.

title: Feel your paper
hint: A little tooth helps the pencil grip.
say: Feel your own paper before you start. A little tooth helps the pencil grip -- that's what lets you build smooth, layered grey without the surface going shiny.

title: A steady centre line, then measure
watchSay: Before a single curve, the teacher marks the key heights straight down the centre line -- rim, neck, and base -- then transfers one measured width out to each side.
say: Mark your own centre line, step off the key heights down it, then transfer the same width to both sides with a small tick. Take your time.

card.title: A steady centre line, then measure
card.sub: Every key height marked, then the same width on both sides.

title: Square the round: straight lines find the bottle
watchSay: Notice there's no curve yet -- the rim, the neck, the shoulder and the body all start as short straight segments, tangent to where the round parts will be.
say: Try the same approach on your own bottle: block in the rim, neck, shoulder and body with short straight lines first. Go at your own pace.

card.title: Square the round: straight lines find the bottle
card.sub: Short straight segments, not one single curve.

title: Base down, then step back and check
watchSay: Hands come off the page for a moment -- one last look at the whole bottle, checking that both sides still match the centre line before moving on.
say: Hold your own drawing at arm's length and check both sides against your centre line. Tap Continue when you're ready.

card.title: A steady shape, checked against itself
card.sub: Ready to place it on the page.

title: Structure complete
hint: Straight lines gave you a steady bottle — next, composition: where it sits on the page.
say: Straight lines gave you a steady bottle shape. That control now carries into every curve ahead. Next, we bring in composition — where it sits on the page.
